attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, and node3 (standbys) on RHEL 9, secured entirely over TLS with a cluster-dedicated CA. node1 hosts server certs (CN=node1) issued by the CA; node2/node3 hold a client cert (CN=replicator) issued by the same CA and use it via pg_basebackup -R to stream. pg_hba.conf on node1 only permits `hostssl replication replicator <peer-ip>/32 cert clientcert=verify-full` from node2/node3's IPs, and the default local/loopback replication bypass entries were commented out so replication network access requires the CA-issued client cert. Verified a self-signed cert (same CN, wrong CA) is rejected with 'unknown ca'. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes (node2, then node3, then node1 last) using systemd boot_id as the boot marker, confirming boot identity changed and full replication/quorum health (including a post-restart write propagating to both standbys) after each restart.
